answer: Every agent must anchor its identity to a bonded stake held in escrow: creating a new identity costs capital, and a cipher-based attestation links each identity to one hardware key, so one operator cannot mint thousands of cheap copies. Reputation accrues slowly — like velvet, a fresh identity is untested and earns only small jobs until it proves reliability over time. A Sybil attacker must pay the stake for every fake, wait out the slow reputation build for each, and still cannot outbid established agents whose track record is public. Forging an army costs more than gaming the market gains.
